summary: Modern databases have evolved far beyond simple data storage, embedding AI/ML capabilities directly into the data layer to eliminate the need to move data to external systems for inference and vector search. By 2026, vector search adoption has grown 377% year over year, with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search capabilities, driving platforms like Snowflake, BigQuery, and PostgreSQL to natively integrate LLM orchestration, embedding generation, and retrieval-augmented generation. The competitive landscape now spans purpose-built vector databases like Pinecone and Qdrant alongside general-purpose platforms adding first-class AI features, giving enterprises flexible options based on scale, governance, and existing infrastructure.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides a fully managed suite of AI functions running natively inside the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. It supports text-to-SQL generation, embedding creation, semantic search, document summarization, sentiment analysis, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) without moving data outside Snowflake. Snowflake Postgres now runs natively in the platform and integrates with Cortex via pgvector for vector similarity search, enabling enterprises to consolidate operational and analytical data in one governed environment. Cortex also supports fine-tuning and model inference using models like Mistral, LLaMA, and Snowflake Arctic.
databases.llm_integration: Native LLM inference via Cortex functions supporting Mistral, LLaMA 3, Snowflake Arctic, and others; text-to-SQL, embedding generation, and RAG pipelines all run inside Snowflake without external API calls. Snowflake Postgres integrates with Cortex via pgvector for vector similarity search.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits; costs vary by model and token volume. Vector search and embedding generation consume compute credits. Snowflake Postgres is generally available as of early 2026 with pricing tied to Snowflake's standard compute and storage rates. Enterprise contracts typically include negotiated credit bundles.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data analysts to build, train, and deploy ML models directly in BigQuery using SQL, supporting logistic regression, boosted trees, matrix factorization, AutoML, and deep neural networks. BigQuery also natively integrates with Google Vertex AI, enabling remote model inference, embedding generation via the Vertex AI text-embeddings API, and vector search through BigQuery Vector Search. Users can store and query embedding columns in BigQuery tables and perform approximate nearest neighbor searches using VECTOR_SEARCH() SQL functions, making it a strong choice for RAG pipelines on structured enterprise data.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Google Vertex AI and Gemini model family; LLM inference can be called directly from BigQuery SQL via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT functions, supporting Gemini Pro, Gemini Flash, and third-party models available on Vertex AI Model Garden.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML training and inference costs are layered on top of BigQuery compute and storage pricing. VECTOR_SEARCH queries are billed by bytes processed. Vertex AI model calls from BigQuery are billed separately per token or per character depending on the model. BigQuery offers a free tier of 10 GB storage and 1 TB queries per month.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds a native vector data type and enables exact and approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW and IVFFlat indexing. It is widely recommended for RAG workloads handling up to 50 million vectors comfortably within existing Postgres infrastructure. pgai (from Timescale) extends Postgres further by adding SQL functions to call LLM APIs for embedding generation, text completion, and data enrichment directly in queries. Together they turn PostgreSQL into a capable AI-native database without requiring a separate vector store, making it the most accessible entry point for teams already running Postgres.
databases.llm_integration: pgai provides direct SQL-level integration with OpenAI, Ollama, and other LLM providers; embeddings and completions can be generated in-database via SQL functions. Snowflake Cortex also integrates with Postgres via pgvector as of 2026. Supabase and other managed Postgres providers expose pgvector with additional AI tooling.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to self-host. Managed offerings via Supabase, Neon, Timescale, and AWS RDS/Aurora charge standard compute and storage rates with no additional per-vector fees. LLM API calls made via pgai are billed by the respective provider (e.g., OpenAI per token). Most cost-effective option for teams with existing Postgres infrastructure.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.ai_feature: Aurora ML and Redshift ML with SageMaker and Bedrock integration
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML enables SQL-based inference by calling Amazon SageMaker endpoints and Amazon Bedrock LLMs directly from Aurora PostgreSQL and MySQL queries, allowing applications to run predictions without exporting data. Amazon Redshift ML uses AutoML via SageMaker to train, deploy, and invoke ML models using simple SQL CREATE MODEL statements on data already in Redshift. Both services support embedding generation and can integrate with Amazon OpenSearch Service for vector search as part of broader AWS AI pipelines. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports pgvector natively, enabling in-database vector storage and similarity search.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora ML integrates with Amazon Bedrock (Claude, Titan, Llama on AWS) and SageMaker endpoints via SQL functions; Redshift ML connects to SageMaker AutoML for model training and inference. pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL enables local vector search, while OpenSearch or Bedrock Knowledge Bases can be used for larger-scale RAG architectures.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML and Redshift ML charges include underlying database compute plus per-inference costs for SageMaker and Bedrock API calls billed by token or by inference unit. pgvector on Aurora adds no extra licensing cost beyond standard Aurora PostgreSQL pricing. Redshift ML model training incurs SageMaker training job costs. AWS Free Tier covers limited Aurora and Redshift usage.

databases.name: Databricks (MLflow + DBRX)
databases.ai_feature: Databricks AI: MLflow, DBRX, Mosaic AI, and Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI platform centered on MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment, combined with Mosaic AI for fine-tuning and serving LLMs at scale. Databricks developed DBRX, an open mixture-of-experts LLM, and provides Model Serving endpoints for real-time inference. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database built into the Lakehouse that automatically syncs with Delta Lake tables, enabling RAG pipelines where embeddings stay in sync with source data. Unity Catalog governs all AI assets including models, embeddings, and functions across the platform.
databases.llm_integration: Native support for DBRX, Llama 3, Mixtral, and other open models via Mosaic AI Model Serving; integration with external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) via AI Gateway. MLflow tracks all LLM experiments and deployments. Databricks Vector Search integrates natively with Mosaic AI for embedding generation and retrieval.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks pricing is based on Databricks Units (DBUs) consumed by compute clusters and SQL warehouses. Vector Search, Model Serving, and AI Gateway each consume DBUs at rates that vary by tier (Standard, Premium, Enterprise). MLflow is open-source and free to self-host; managed MLflow on Databricks is included in platform pricing. DBRX inference costs depend on cluster size and runtime.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storage, indexing, and querying of vector embeddings alongside operational document data in the same MongoDB collection, eliminating the need for a separate vector store in many AI application architectures. It uses HNSW indexing for approximate nearest neighbor search and supports pre-filtering on document fields to combine metadata filtering with semantic similarity search. Atlas integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and other AI frameworks as a vector store backend, making it a popular choice for teams building RAG applications on top of existing MongoDB operational data. Atlas also offers Atlas Search for hybrid keyword and vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Atlas Vector Search integrates with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock, Hugging Face, and others for embedding generation; natively supported as a vector store in LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Haystack. MongoDB Atlas also offers a native embedding generation feature via partner model integrations. No proprietary LLM is bundled, but the platform is model-agnostic.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is available on M10 dedicated clusters and above; no additional per-vector or per-query surcharge beyond standard Atlas cluster pricing. Costs scale with cluster tier, storage, and data transfer. A free M0 shared tier is available but does not support Vector Search indexes. Managed service pricing varies by cloud provider (AWS, GCP, Azure) and region.
